summary.text: Debra Hobbs is an independent candidate for the Arkansas House of Representatives, District 45, in the November 3, 2026 general election, where she faces incumbent Republican Aaron Pilkington.
A former school counselor, teacher and small business owner, she served in the Arkansas House as a Republican from 2009 to 2015.

paragraphs.text: Debra Hobbs earned a B.S. in science composite from the University of the Ozarks in 1977 and an M.S. in counseling education from the University of Arkansas in 1987.
Ballotpedia lists her professional experience as a school counselor and teacher and as a small business owner.
Hobbs was elected to the Arkansas House of Representatives in 2008, running unopposed in the general election, and won re-election without opposition in 2010 and 2012.

Ballotpedia lists her as having represented District 94 from 2009 to 2015; her committee assignments in the 2013 session included Education, State Agencies and Governmental Affairs, Legislative Council and Joint Performance Review.
She ran in the 2014 Republican primary for lieutenant governor and finished third with 16 percent of the vote, behind Tim Griffin and Andy Mayberry.
In 2016 she ran in the Republican primary for House District 94, losing to incumbent Rebecca Petty, 57.7 percent to 42.3 percent.
